title: PrismPaperBurn skips the ember flicker noise and ember maths where the ember is exactly zero (outside the char band, or before ignition)
runtimeWriters: Only _Burn is written at runtime: PrismBurnView.cs:203-228 stamps per instance (progress 0..1, e.Seed, coverage near*a or (1-near)*a, flags 0/+1 MID/+2 NoHoles) and Submit (PrismBurnView.cs:244-255) draws it with Graphics.RenderMeshInstanced through a MaterialPropertyBlock. Every other property (_EmberWidth 0.035, _CharWidth 0.11, _ScorchWidth 0.22, _Span 1.3, _EmberFlicker 0.35, _NoiseAmount 0.38, _NoiseFreq 4.5) is the .mat's: grep of each name across Assets/_Scripts finds no writer. The laser burn (PrismLaserBurn.mat) uses another shader and is untouched.
exposure: Drawn by PrismBurnManager (EnsureInstance, PrismBurnManager.cs:88) for every prism burning in the paper style: the Grizzly flamethrower (GrizzlyFlamethrowerActionExecutor.cs:119). NEAR tier (PrismPaperBurnNear.mat, _BURN_CURL) close up, MID tier (PrismPaperBurnMid.mat) further out, every platform tier. Only while prisms burn.

signoff.heading: Paper burn sign-off
signoff.subject: the burning-paper look a prism takes when the Grizzly's flame catches it
signoff.whatChanged: The glowing ember edge and the faint smoulder behind it are only ever visible near the burn. Everywhere else they add exactly nothing, but the shader still worked out a flicker noise for every pixel. Now it skips that work where the glow is zero. The glow itself is drawn exactly as before.
signoff.frameNote: Material PrismPaperBurnNear on a cube, burned about half way, seen from many angles. The ember glow is the thin bright edge round the hole; look there in the 1:1 view.
notMeasured: Its share of a real frame: it only costs anything while prisms are burning.
